resources.string: Reads the text currently on screen when you press the accessibility button or invoke Hiroi as assistant, so you can copy it or look it up. Nothing is stored or sent anywhere.
Hiroi grabs the text on your screen so you can copy it or send it to your dictionary app, even where an app doesn\'t let you select text.
Sideloaded app? If the switch is greyed out, open App info, tap ⋮ and choose \"Allow restricted settings\" first.
2. Optional: make Hiroi your digital assistant app
Then long-pressing the power button (or swiping up from a bottom corner) opens Hiroi. Enable \"Use text from screen\" in the same settings page.

Import Yomitan dictionaries (.zip), the same files desktop Yomitan uses: e.g. Jitendex or JMdict for definitions, JPDB for frequency, Kanjium for pitch accent, KANJIDIC for kanji. Dictionaries higher up in the list are shown first; ▲▼ change the order. Untick a dictionary to turn it off without removing it.

A collection is all dictionaries in one file, ready to use: importing one onto another phone (or this one again) takes no parsing, so it\'s much faster than importing each dictionary. It adds the dictionaries that aren\'t here yet, after these, on or off as they were. ▲▼ set the order: dictionaries higher up come first in the results, as in Yomitan.
Already here, left as they are: %s
All dictionaries are turned off. Turn one on in the Hiroi app.
The name to show for the dictionary %s, in this list and in results:
The place to move %1$s to, 1 to %2$d:
Searches with an asterisk first (*べる: the words ending in べる) work with every dictionary in Hiroi; it gets them ready the first time one is searched.
The dictionary\'s forms of other words (a past tense, another spelling or reading) find those words, as in Yomitan.
%d of its terms are such forms.
It was imported before Hiroi used them: import it again (or update it) to use any it has.

As in Yomitan: results are sorted by how much of the text they match, then by fewer conjugation steps, then by this frequency list, then by dictionary order. A list counts as ranks (lower = more common) or occurrence counts (higher = more common) as its index.json says; otherwise Hiroi compares its values for common and rare words, as Yomitan does.
Import a frequency list (e.g. JPDB, BCCWJ) to sort by it.
As in Yomitan: 🔊 plays the word from the first source that has it, in this order. Long-press 🔊 to see every source and pick a recording; the one picked is also what a card\'s {audio} gets.
Play the first result\'s audio when results show

{term}, {reading} and {language} (ja) are filled in. A Custom URL is the audio itself; a JSON one answers with {\"type\": \"audioSourceList\", \"audioSources\": [{\"url\": …, \"name\": …}]}, as for Yomitan (e.g. a local audio server).
No Japanese text-to-speech on this phone. Install a voice (e.g. Google\'s speech services) or use another source.
Freeze the screen while Hiroi is open
Hiroi shows the screen as it was when you triggered it, so a notification or toast that closes itself, a video or an animation stays where its text was. Apps that forbid screenshots stay live.

All of Hiroi\'s settings in one file, to move them to another phone or keep a copy: Anki and card formats with their templates, marks, audio, translation, sorting, and the dictionaries\' order and switches (the dictionaries themselves go in a collection: see Dictionaries). Importing replaces the settings here.
Without them, the file is safe to share; importing it keeps the keys the other phone has.
Settings exported, with API keys: keep the file private.
Replace Hiroi\'s settings with the ones from this file?\n\n%1$s
It has no API keys: the ones here are kept.
Settings imported. Not installed here (import them to use their order): %1$s

The panel and the search page offer a translation of what you read: the sentence of the word you looked up, the text you selected, or all of it. Long-press the translation for other services. Cards can have it too, with {sentence-translation}.
Tried in this order until one has a translation. Tap a service with a key or address to change it.
No translation service is set up
An API key from deepl.com (API Free: 500,000 characters a month). The text you translate goes to DeepL.
A LibreTranslate server, e.g. your own. libretranslate.com needs an API key. The text you translate goes to that server.
API key (if the server wants one)
A URL that answers with the translation, as text or JSON. {text} is the text, {source} ja and {target} the language to translate into. The text you translate goes there.
Downloading the on-device translation model (about 30 MB)…
Couldn\'t translate. Tap to try again.\n%1$s
not downloaded (about 30 MB, downloaded on first use)
None of the dictionaries can be updated: their index.json has no update links (Jitendex, JMdict, JMnedict, KANJIDIC and Jiten have them; import them again if they came before Hiroi kept them).
Download and import the new versions? %1$s\n\nEach one replaces the old one once it\'s imported, keeping its place, its switch and the settings that name it. Big dictionaries take a few minutes.
You\'re on mobile data: Jitendex and JMdict are big downloads.
No updates: its index.json has no update links.

When deinflecting words, only entries whose part of speech matches what the deinflector expects are shown (as in Yomitan). Turn it off for dictionaries that don\'t say the part of speech, so conjugated words find their entries too.

As Yomitan\'s result grouping mode. No grouping: every definition is a separate entry. Group term-reading pairs: definitions for the same term with the same reading together. Group by term: definitions for the same term together, whatever the reading. Group related terms: related terms that share the same definitions together (other spellings, kana forms).
The primary dictionary should be one with related term information (e.g. JMdict or Jitendex); the secondary dictionaries add their definitions for the related terms.
Compress the frequency tags into one \"Average\" tag, the harmonic mean of each list\'s value, as Yomitan\'s option does. Lists of occurrence counts are left out of it.

Trigger Hiroi with the accessibility button, the accessibility shortcut, or the assistant gesture, then tap a word in one of the boxes to look it up. Text in pictures is read with OCR as soon as Hiroi opens and gets a dashed box. Drag over the screen to take just the text in that region. In the panel, long-press to select text yourself; Share sends the word, sentence, box or selection to the clipboard, an app, DeepL, ChatGPT and so on, and \"Look up\" opens it in a dictionary app. Long-press \"Look up\" to pick a different app.

Shows whether a looked-up word already has a note in one of your Anki decks, and adds cards. For \"Open in Anki\", switch AnkiDroid\'s card browser to \"All decks\" once: it only searches the deck it last showed.
AnkiDroid with AnkiConnect Android running, or desktop Anki with the AnkiConnect add-on (enter its address, e.g. http://192.168.0.20:8765).
Hiroi uses AnkiDroid\'s own API for other apps: no AnkiConnect Android needed. AnkiDroid makes every change itself. It must have been opened once, and Hiroi needs its permission.
AnkiDroid isn\'t installed, or is too old to have its API.
Hiroi may not use AnkiDroid yet: allow it in Hiroi → Anki.
Not allowed. If Android doesn\'t ask any more, allow it in Android\'s settings for Hiroi: Permissions → Additional permissions → AnkiDroid.
Lookups show whether a word has a note in %1$s (field %2$s).

Add notes from the overlay with \"＋ Anki\". Fields are filled by Yomitan\'s own Anki card templates, with its markers ({expression}, {glossary}, {sentence}, …) and your own, so you can take your card format and templates from Yomitan.
No Anki card formats with a note type in that file.

Each field is text with markers such as {expression} or {glossary}, filled by the Anki card templates as Yomitan fills them. {…} lists the markers: Yomitan\'s, one per dictionary ({single-glossary-…}), and those your templates add.

The Handlebars templates that fill the fields, Yomitan\'s own (%s): every {marker} is the template of that name ({{#*inline \"expression\"}}…{{/inline}}), filled from the looked-up word as in Yomitan. Change them, or add your own markers, as described in Yomitan\'s docs (docs/templates.md). Changes are saved as you leave this page.
Compact glossaries (Yomitan\'s \"Compact Popup and Anki\" layout)
Compact tags (only tags that differ from the previous definition\'s)
毎日、日本語を勉強しています。
No dictionary entry for that text.
Replace the templates with Yomitan\'s default ones? Your own markers in them are lost.
Fields are filled with Yomitan\'s default templates (%s).
Fields are filled with your own templates (Yomitan %s).
Check for duplicates (notes with the same first field)
its top deck with all subdecks
Count notes of every note type
As in Yomitan: results that would duplicate a note show it on their button (\"Already in Anki\", \"Overwrite\" or \"＋ Anki again\") and get \"Open in Anki\".

resources.string: Word audio for {audio}, from the audio sources
Dictionary styles once in the note type, not in every card

Yomitan\'s templates copy each dictionary\'s whole stylesheet into every card (tens of KB per card, which can push a collection over AnkiWeb\'s limit). With this on, Hiroi takes those rules out of new cards and keeps them here: copy them with \"Note type CSS…\" and paste them at the end of the note type\'s Styling (Anki: Note types → Cards → Styling), or let Hiroi put them there (below), or the cards lose the dictionaries\' styles. Same as the anki-yomitan-css-dedup add-on, which shares that section.
Paste this at the end of the note type\'s Styling, replacing the section between the same BEGIN and END lines if it\'s already there. %1$d dictionaries, %2$s.
No dictionary styles yet: they\'re collected from the cards you make with this on.
The dictionary styles changed since you last copied them: copy them again and replace the section in the note type.
The note type has the latest styles, if you pasted what you copied.
Let Hiroi update the note type\'s Styling

Whenever the styles change, Hiroi adds them to the Styling of the card format\'s note type, in that section, and keeps the rest of the Styling (and sheets already in the section) as it is. Desktop Anki (AnkiConnect) and AnkiDroid on this phone can; AnkiConnect Android can\'t.
Note type %s now has the dictionary styles.
Note type %s already had the dictionary styles.
Choose the card format\'s note type first.
Note type %s has the latest styles.
Note type %s gets the latest styles with the next card, or with \"Update note type\".
Note type %s\'s Styling now has the new dictionary styles
Card added, but the note type\'s Styling wasn\'t updated: %s
The dictionary styles for the note type changed: copy them again (Hiroi → Anki → Note type CSS…)
{screenshot}: just the box or region, not the whole screen
\"＋ Anki\" adds %1$s notes to %2$s (%3$d fields filled).
Choose a deck and note type, or import your card format from Yomitan.
Not defined in the templates, these come out as {…-render-error}: %s

Type or paste Japanese: a word, as written or conjugated (食べさせられた), or a whole sentence. Romaji works too (taberu, TEREBI for katakana) while a→あ is on. Results are for the text from its first character; tap another character in the text above to look up the word starting there.

English or German finds the words whose definitions have it (eat, essen), in the dictionaries with definitions in it; with a→あ on, what reads as romaji in full shows its Japanese words first. If nothing is found, what's one letter away is: wter finds water, tbaeru 食べる.

An asterisk searches for words starting or ending with the text, as written: 食べ* finds 食べる, 食べ物, …, and *べる finds 食べる, 調べる, …

You can also select text in any app and choose "Hiroi search" in the selection menu.
Type Japanese text to search for.
None of the dictionaries turned on can be searched in English or German. Dictionaries with English or German definitions imported before Hiroi could search them by meaning need importing again.
Type text before the * to find words starting with it, or after it for words ending with it.
Preparing suffix search, once: this takes a while with big dictionaries…
Like AnkiMark: words with a note in Anki get a colour in the overlay, by rule (new, learning, mature, …), and the bar shows how much of the screen\'s text you know.

Words you have notes for in Anki are marked in Hiroi\'s boxes and in the panel, in the colour of the first rule they match, as AnkiMark does on web pages. The AnkiConnect address and API key are the ones under Anki on the main screen.
Searches or fields changed since the last sync.
No base filter set, so rules search your whole collection.
Put in front of every rule, usually your deck. Any Anki search works, e.g. deck:\"Japanese::Vocab\" -is:suspended. Leave it empty to search your whole collection.

Each rule is an Anki search plus a colour. A word gets the colour of the first rule (top to bottom) that one of its notes matches. Notes matching no rule aren\'t marked. Card searches like is:due match a note if any of its cards match.
Anki search (empty = everything in the base filter)
Replace all rules with the default new / learning / mature rules?
Which note fields hold the Japanese word. With none ticked, each note\'s first field is used.
Tap \"Load fields\" to list the fields of your notes.
Add a base filter or a rule search first.

For words that a field holds among other things, such as the other spellings in a dictionary entry: JavaScript that gets the note and returns a list of words. They\'re added to the fields\' words and cleaned the same way. note.fields maps each field name to its HTML; there are also note.modelName, note.tags and note.noteId. DOMParser works; network access doesn\'t. Leave it empty for none.
Match conjugated forms (食べなかった → 食べる)
Finds verbs and adjectives in any form (past, negative, polite, て-form, passive, causative, potential, …) and marks the whole word. Off: only words written exactly as in your notes.
Match kana words in either script (ゴミ ↔ ごみ)

A note written only in kana also matches the word in the other kana (ハマる also matches はまる). A note with the other spelling itself takes precedence. Can mark the odd unrelated word, e.g. まま for a note ママ.
When marking is on, it can still be off for single apps. The overlay\'s Marks button switches it everywhere or for the app you\'re in.

resources.string: A sync only reads notes that are new or edited since the last one (AnkiConnect Android: new ones, plus everything once a day), so frequent syncs stay cheap. The overlay marks with the last sync\'s words meanwhile.
How many notes a sync reads from Anki at once (default 100). Lower it if AnkiConnect Android stops during a sync; desktop Anki copes with more.

Save these settings as a JSON file, or load them from one. Files exported from AnkiMark work too, and AnkiMark can import Hiroi\'s. Importing replaces the settings found in the file. The Anki address and API key are not included.
Imported settings%s. Sync once to use them.
It includes a field script; check what it does before syncing.

Open Hiroi on this screen (power button or accessibility button) and tap a word in one of the sentences below. The last one is a picture, not text: Hiroi reads it with OCR in the background and adds a dashed box. The example dictionary has every word in them, with definitions from Jitendex (jitendex.org, CC BY-SA 4.0).
